g.text: 89% of spawning nights fall while the sea
is warming, just 47% of the year
68% fall in the 8 days after full moon,
Half of all spawning starts between

rect.style: stroke-width: 1.07; stroke: none; stroke-linecap: butt; stroke-linejoin: miter; fill: #FF7E8B;

g.text: White line: average time. Length R: 0 = evenly spread, 1 = all at one moment
Corals do not spawn at random. Each clock shows when they spawn: in the year, in the Moon’s cycle and in the day.
The reef reads three clocks, and the Moon is the loosest
R (mean resultant length) shows how concentrated the records are. It is not a confidence interval. Spawning is not watched equally at all times, so quiet times are under-recorded.
884 spawning nights on the year clock, 1,026 on the Moon clock, 346 timed starts on the Sun clock. Sources: Baird et al. (2021), NOAA Coral Reef Watch.
